Not One But a Couple of Reborn Pontiac GTO Muscle Cars Dwell Around a Fictional Race Track in the US
11 photos
Photo: angelguerradesign / Instagram
Even casual automotive fans have probably heard at least once about the iconic Pontiac GTO. But how many people know about its absolute importance for the American muscle car movement?
This model was crucial to the development of the American muscle car sector in particular and for sports cars at large, with the Pontiac GTO being originally a front-engine, rear-wheel drive, two-door, and four-passenger automobile manufactured across just five generations (with a hiatus between 1975 and 2003) from 1963 to 2006. More precisely, the first iteration is establishing the nameplate's quirky 'nose' and also, at large, for popularizing the incipient muscle car market segment during the 1960s.
The Pontiac GTO was different from the Ford Mustang, as the latter was smaller and more compact, but also cheaper, and it created the pony car niche, which always slotted below the muscle cars even though in recent times the boundaries have blurred via stuff like the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC or the 2027 Dodge Charger Super Bee, among others.
Back to the Pontiac GTO, the definitive iteration that’s enshrined in popular culture is the second generation, which was produced from 1968 to 1972 and had semi-fastback two-door hardtop, coupe, and convertible body styles. This one had all sorts of cool models, including ‘ The Judge .’ As such, it is no wonder that people haven't forgotten about it, right?
That includes the imaginative realm of digital car content creators, as the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are always ready to draw from nostalgia – sometimes more than once. For example, Angel Guerra, a virtual artist better known as angelguerradesign on social media, who has prior experience in automotive design via Bugatti and Rimac, among others, digitally proposed us more than two years ago a modern Pontiac GTO revival.
Even better, the pixel master created both The Judge Pontiac GTO revival as well as a more extreme GTO-R version that could easily muster the courage to fight the Ford Mustang GTD without a second’s thought. Now the CGI expert has decided to circle back to his reborn GTO and show it off with additional colors: red, blue, white, or gray – with or without the racing stripes for some of them.
So, what do you think? Should General Motors bring back the Pontiac GTO for an extreme sports car that’s capable of standing up to the S650 Ford Mustang GTD and its 5.2-liter supercharged V8 churning out no less than 815 horsepower? After all, they have the powertrain know-how to make it happen, as all they have to do is ask Team Corvette to lend them one of the options from the C8 Grand Sport, Grand Sport X, Z06, or the ZR1 and ZR1X.
